objective: Does adding a differentiable topology-fidelity loss on the decoder's reconstruction, on top of D_full's unmodified recipe, converge without instability? (Section 5 real-data gate)
decision_rule: PASS iff 0 NaN/Inf steps AND mean(loss_total) over the second half of the final 20% of steps <= mean(loss_total) over the first half of that same window -- same rule as pretrain_dirac_job.py's own Gate 3, applied to this run's total_loss (which now includes LAM_TD * loss_topology_diff)
interpretation: Full run: 13300 steps across 50 epochs over 533 cases, lam_td=0.01. 0 NaN/Inf steps. total_loss fell from 0.7402 (first 20%) to 0.2174 (final 20%), and within that final-20% window kept decreasing. loss_topology_diff fell from 0.4621 to 0.3637 over the same window (PASS/FAIL is decided on total_loss alone, per decision_rule -- this number is diagnostic, not gate-critical). Mean added gudhi wall time per step: 1.30s.
